institutionalProjectStatus.source: Silliman University Angelo King Center for Research and Environmental Management (SUAKCREM), Monthly Report, June–September 2024.
institutionalProjectStatus.finding: The report says SUAKCREM and Central Mindanao University researchers held planning on 30 September 2024 for 2025 research at Balinsasayao Twin Lakes. It states that the Protected Area Management Board had approved Dr. R. S. Guino-o's proposal titled “Assessment of Water Profile, Plankton, Macroinvertebrates, and Fish Assemblage of BTLNP.”
institutionalProjectStatus.completedDataset: The report records approval and planning, not completed sampling or fish results. No final project report, species-by-station table, survey dates, effort or voucher list was located in this review.

historicalAgencyInventoryLead.source: Palaubsanon, M. L. (2012, June 19). DENR-7: Alien species invade nat'l park in Negros Oriental. The Freeman / Philstar.com.
historicalAgencyInventoryLead.finding: The news report attributes a three-day DENR-7 inventory conducted 13–15 June 2012 to the regional Ecosystems Research and Development Services and names Tilapia mossambica, Gambusia affinis, and Cyprinus carpio as fish found in the lakes.
historicalAgencyInventoryLead.limitations: These are names as printed in secondary news, not independently taxonomically validated here. The primary inventory report, exact lake-by-lake localities, fish methods, specimens, identification records and item-specific reuse terms were not found. The news item is not a primary checklist or evidence of current presence.

priorBroadChecklist.source: Bucol and Carumbana's 2010 Negros–Siquijor freshwater/brackish checklist, separately reviewed in national-visayas-negros-siquijor-2010-checklist-scope-review-20261030.json.
priorBroadChecklist.finding: That broad tentative checklist mentions a carp as introduced to the twin lakes, but its aggregate island list is not a current or complete lake inventory and does not replace the pending fish-assemblage study.

otherParkInventory.source: Amoroso et al. (2017), Biodiversity Inventory and Assessment in Balinsasayao Twin Lakes Natural Park, Transactions of the National Academy of Science and Technology (Philippines), 39(1), 73.
otherParkInventory.finding: The search-indexed abstract describes a two-hectare permanent-plot/adjacent-area vertebrate inventory of birds, mammals, reptiles and amphibians; it reports no fish group or fish checklist and therefore cannot fill the lake-fish gap. The full proceedings PDF was not retrievable in the viewer.

2023ProjectStatus.source: Silliman University Annual Report 2023, indexed text for the CHED-funded BioConUP project.
2023ProjectStatus.finding: The report describes a CMU-led biodiversity-monitoring project at a two-hectare permanent plot and says the project was awaiting renewal of the protected-area Gratuitous Permit before fieldwork. It provides no fish-assemblage results in the reviewed excerpt.
2023ProjectStatus.limitations: This is permanent-plot project-status evidence, not a lake-specific fish inventory. The full PDF was too large for the page viewer; no fish-results table was located.

decision.use: Treat the SUAKCREM report as a high-priority institutional follow-up lead for a planned fish assemblage survey; treat the 2012 news report only as a dated secondary lead to locate the original DENR-7 inventory.
decision.reason: The institutional report documents an approved proposal, not results. A 2012 secondary report names three fish taxa from the lakes but supplies no lake-specific or specimen-level evidence; the prior checklist is tentative and broad.

limitations: Balinsasayao and Danao are separate lakes; park-wide or watershed-level evidence must not be silently assigned to both lake waterbodies.
PAMB approval of a proposal is not proof that the project ran, that fish were sampled, or that any taxon was observed.
The 2012 press report does not distinguish which fish record came from which lake or provide methods, stations, vouchers or coordinates.
The 2010 Negros–Siquijor checklist calls its island-wide list tentative and does not provide a current, complete twin-lakes baseline.
The NAST permanent-plot summary's listed vertebrate groups do not include fish; do not treat its overall inventory count as fish richness.
No current presence, abundance, native status, catchability, diet, legal advice, water safety, map boundary or regional completeness is established here.

Three scientific names are preserved only as printed in a secondary 2012 news report; they are not taxonomically validated, promoted to current occurrences, or added as public app rows. No map geometry, diet records, safety alerts, or public app rows were added.
nextActions: Ask SUAKCREM and Central Mindanao University whether the PAMB-approved 2025 fish-assemblage project proceeded and whether a final report, survey schedule, stations, gear/effort, taxon list, voucher details and permitted reuse terms are available.
Ask DENR Region VII/PAMO-BTLNP for the June 2012 invasive-alien-species inventory report and exact lake-specific fish observations rather than deriving a checklist from the press item.

Continue the Siaton River source trail: obtain Carumbana's cited 2006 unpublished report, its sampling stations and taxon evidence; keep it distinct from the 2004–2005 Siaton collections summarized in the 2010 checklist.
Search for a primary fish inventory for Lake Balanan separately; do not infer fish taxa from tourism, general lake-conservation or water-quality reports.

references.supports: SUAKCREM's institutional record of the 30 September 2024 planning meeting, a 2025 BTLNP research plan and PAMB approval of the fish-assemblage proposal; it contains no project fish results.
Secondary news report about a June 2012 DENR-7 IAS inventory in the twin-lakes park; use only as a lead to locate the primary inventory report.
NAST 2017 biodiversity-inventory abstract for the permanent plot and adjacent areas; the listed vertebrate groups are birds, mammals, reptiles and amphibians, not a fish checklist.
Silliman University's record of a separate 2023 CHED-funded LTER biodiversity-monitoring project at the two-hectare park plot; no fish-assemblage results are reported in the reviewed excerpt.
